flags.message: JBD total 455h runs hot against the takeoff: floor system 87h for 430 sf incl. 25h soffit, wall framing 28h @0.45 h/LF for 63 LF, and drywall finish 43h are each 20-40% above card-rate arithmetic even after the canon +20-25% elevated premium; treat the JBD as a ceiling, not a target.

JBD double-counts WRB labor (6h sheathing+WRB line plus a separate 3h WRB line) and prices the 3 dump runs in both Material and Equipment ($2,700 for a 3-run scope); deduct the 3h and one $1,350 when cross-checking.

JBD drywall scope is mis-shaped, not just hot: it carries 848 sf as 504 sf framed walls + 344 sf over brick, but the brick wall is settled as exposed (−344 sf) while the ceiling is settled as finished (+430 sf drywall + 430 sf vented rafter-bay insulation with baffles, 0h in the JBD); total area is a near-wash (~934 vs 848 sf) but overhead sloped-ceiling hang and baffle/batt installation are harder work than the wall hours the JBD priced.

Plate height of 8 ft is a JBD assumption adopted pending field verification; because the EXISTING shed roof is reseated, actual plate height is dictated by the existing bearing line, so sheathing (504 sf), WRB, siding, wall batt and wall drywall are all provisional until the bearing height is measured.

Footer pockets are settled as hand-dug with 4 of 8 saw-cut through the existing pad, but the JBD prices no saw, no cutting hours and only 12h for all footers; groundwork should carry ~1h/pocket hand-dig plus ~1.5h per cut (card) and cite the machine-access deviation, with the 3-5 range still open until the pad is exposed.

JBD roof section (24h) still carries 2 shingle PATCHES, but the settled scope reuses those two penetrations as exhaust vents and adds eave intake for the vented ceiling; vent flashing and ~43 LF of intake venting replace the patch work and are priced nowhere — the hours roughly wash but the materials (2 roof vents, intake strip) do not appear in the takeoff.

Receptacle count is ambiguous between sources: the JBD's 10 outlets is a room total, while the answer describes ~10 on the 43 ft brick wall alone under NEC 210.52 (whose 12-ft rule yields ~4 on that wall); carried as 10 total with the brick-wall share in 43 LF of surface raceway, which the JBD did not price — rough-in gains raceway run/anchoring hours.

Presentation set (5-26-26) still carries stale scope — 7 posts on p3, 7 windows incl. two 5050s, a 6568 double door in the brick wall, 'Drywall over brick', deck/stairs, gable/hip roofs — all settled to the signed proposal by user answers; nothing from it is adopted, and the 3068 door is the only exterior door.

Subpanel conversion kit ($180 + breakers) is contingent on an electrician assessment not yet done; if the fused disconnect is unsuitable, a new subpanel is an add with hours and lead time outside this takeoff, and the mini-split circuit depends on it. Demo is unaffected — the disconnect sits on the house side and survives untouched (settled).

Permits and inspections are contracted-in by the proposal but carry zero hours in the JBD and the permit is not yet applied for (AHJ defaulted to City of Kingsport); with electrical + mechanical rough this job needs footing, framing, electrical rough, mechanical, insulation and final visits (~6 × 2h per card) plus permit lead time ahead of the 2027-03-01 start.

JBD carries 2 scaffold days total, but settled access is scaffold from sloped grade for demo debris lowering, hand-dug footers, post/beam/floor framing, under-floor soffit, siding and roof tie-in; canon bills scaffold erect/strike once on site prep and covers moves via the elevated premium — the JBD prices neither, so the premium must be applied on top of its ground-calibrated lines.

general_conditions is split across main_demolition and structural_framing because shoring must stand from before demo until the roof is reseated on new walls; PM 8h in that section is overhead and should not inflate either component's crew-hours.

The JBD floor_system section carries 25h of vinyl soffit under the floor; it is mapped to cladding_roof (exterior, overhead from scaffold, installed after rough-in per answer) rather than structural_framing so interior-concurrency limits and elevated premiums apply correctly.
